correctness.rationale: For every positive finite model parameter and centered finite-fourth reset law the regenerative stationary state exists with integrable fourth moment. Its exact generator yields V=[2/(q+g+1)+qx]/(q+2) and F=[12V/(q+g+3)+qy]/(q+4), mean zero. Jensen y>=x² is equality-rigid at the unique centered fair binary law. Eliminating x gives K=A+B/V+A V0²/V² on V>=V0. Its derivative has exactly one interior minimum when (q-1)(q+g)<3 and is strictly negative otherwise, proving the global sharp phases and nonattained infimum. The exact optimizer formula gives the square-root critical law. Three-point laws give all attainable kurtoses. Standalone checker independently ran 2,932 assertions; simulation is supplementary, not an infinite proof. No unverified nonstandard lemma is needed.

originality.rationale: A source with exactly the same physical process, Olsen (2023), already establishes every raw moment via Eqs (36)-(42); the new claim is not that recurrence. The evaluated contribution is the global all-centered-reset-law stationary kurtosis minimizer, unique fair binary optimizer, exact parameter boundary between attained and unattained optima, attainable ranges, and square-root divergence of the optimal reset distance. Inspection of source Sec IV and conclusion did not show this optimization. The matched generic published-finding corpus findings concern different objects and invariants. value.rationale: The optimized objective is the natural dimensionless stationary positional kurtosis of a harmonic active-particle model already motivated by literature on variable-position resetting. The theorem determines which reset distributions suppress non-Gaussian fourth-moment shape most effectively across every centered input measure, locates the sharp transition from a practical finite optimal reset radius to a mathematically unattainable infinite-distance infimum, and quantifies how the optimum deteriorates near the threshold. It is a complete global continuous-parameter feasibility classification rather than a routine fixed-parameter computation or known moment-table value. No claims about extreme-tail probabilities or experimental sampling precision are made.
